headline: Triangle runs warm — break slides west to Santa Rosa
body:
Wednesday leads with the small-craft advisory: the outer waters and the Santa Rosa zone sat under SCA into this morning, seas out there 6 to 9 ft and the Flats showing 6.6 ft at midday. The east channel behind the islands is soft, 2–4 ft, and the triangle middle runs about 4.7 ft. Thursday is the sea day — light winds at dawn, seas subsiding toward 3.5 ft in the triangle, with W building to 10–12 kt at the islands by afternoon.

The bluefin problem: the triangle is a warm bathtub both days. West corner 71, east 72, south point 71.2 today, all a touch warmer tomorrow — no 64–68 water anywhere inside it. The break has slid off west. The only cool-side water is Santa Rosa Flats, 67.7 today inside the band, warming to 69 tomorrow. Today that water is right but the ride's ugly; tomorrow the Flats lay down but the edge creeps warm. If it's a day, it's Thursday — run the ~40 nm to the Flats and work the cool edge. Don't grid the triangle on temperature.
